name: Nebraska
status_why: The CSV exports answered scripts; Nov 3 is loaded with zero votes.
system: Secretary of State's own ASP.NET results site on Azure Government (resultsSW.aspx, resultsCSV.aspx, ResultsExport.aspx; data service neresultswebservice.azurewebsites.us). Same platform family as New Mexico's.

results_page.label: Nebraska Secretary of State: election results

feeds.address: https://electionresults.nebraska.gov/resultsCSV.aspx?text=All&type=CG&map=DIST (type codes from the home page: SW statewide, CG Congress, LD Legislature, PS Public Service Commission, SE State Board of Education, RG Regents, JD judicial retention, CC community college, LC Learning Community, NR natural resources districts, UT Metropolitan Utilities District, PP public power districts, RD reclamation districts, ED educational service units, PA statewide ballot measures)
feeds.updates: as counties upload on election night; each row carries CurrentDateTime; results began posting at 8 p.m. CT in 2024
feeds.note: HTTP 200 application/text on 2026-10-09. Columns: RaceID, RaceName, PartyCode, AreaType, AreaNum, OfficeSeqNo, BallotOrder, CandidateID, CandidateName, CurrentDateTime, VoteFor, CandidateVotes, CandidatePercentage, PrecinctsReporting (e.g. ='0/438'). Already set up for the Nov 3 general with zero votes.
Same export pattern as Congress; not requested separately.

feeds.address: https://electionresults.nebraska.gov/ResultsExport.aspx?cat=SWALL: 'Statewide Export', 'Legislative Export' and one export per county, each an ASP.NET postback (__doPostBack with __VIEWSTATE)
feeds.note: Page answered 200; the postback itself was not tried. Header fields show 1,322 precincts and 1,259,447 registered voters.

feeds.address: https://neresultswebservice.azurewebsites.us/ (the map service the page calls; New Mexico's twin has GetMapDataArchive?type=..&category=CTY)
feeds.note: County-by-county figures for the map. The method name for the live election has not been confirmed.

races_in_feed: State Board of Education, Regents, PSC
special districts (NRD, MUD, public power, ESU, community college, Learning Community)
local: Yes, for county, city and school races. The state hosts county files at countyelectionresults.nebraska.gov/election_files/<County>/ (for example .../Hall/2026_Primary_unofficial_results.pdf). Douglas County: votedouglascounty-ne.gov. Lancaster: lancaster.ne.gov (Election Commissioner). Sarpy: sarpy.gov. These sites were not requested.
how_counted: Counties upload their counts from 8 p.m. Central.
count_order: No vote-type columns in the CSV.
vote_types: Not in the CSV seen (no early/absentee/election-day columns). The canvass book gives totals only. Count order would need county sources.

certify.body: the Nebraska Board of State Canvassers
certify.rule: Meets on the fourth Monday after the election (Neb. Rev. Stat. 32-1037).
certify.local_rule: Counties send abstracts after their canvass (32-1034).
certify.source: NCSL, 'Election Certification Deadlines' (www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/certification-deadlines), read 2026-10-10; secondary: a summary of each state's law, not the law itself

rehearsal: The posted zero-vote exports (structure and crosswalk); no past election is served by this site. New Mexico's twin system is replayed for the reader.
terms: None stated on the pages read.
scout_plan: Nebraska is one of the easiest. On election night the updater can read the CSV exports for SW, CG, LD and the other type codes every few minutes (a handful of small files) and match RaceID and CandidateID to the ballot rows already loaded. County-by-county numbers for the map come from the per-county exports (a form postback) or the map service. Local city and school results are county by county: start with the state-hosted county files and Douglas and Lancaster's own sites.
notes: Nov 3 already loaded with zeros: a zero report is not a result.
The CSV's CurrentDateTime column is the server's clock when asked, not the time of the figures; the reader leaves it out of the version and the figures carry the time they were fetched.
sources: NCSL, 'Election Certification Deadlines' (www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/certification-deadlines), read 2026-10-10; secondary: a summary of each state's law, not the law itself
